liminal_instructions.ship_drive: We've found Instructions that bend space-time, compressing and expanding space around a Linkage. Unfortunately, hyperspace is too unstable for this to speed up travel, but I'm sure you can imagine the combat applications.
liminal_instructions.bad_missile: We can create a field that absorbs explosive energy, reducing missile rate of fire, but stabilizing the Linkage.
liminal_instructions.bad_energy: By diffusing energy weapon outputs across space-time, we decrease their rate of fire and increase flux requirements, but make the entire system more stable.
liminal_instructions.bad_ballistic: A field that interferes with ballistic weapon systems slows their rate of fire and increases flux requirements, but we can harness that energy for other purposes.
liminal_instructions.bad_flux: By redirecting some of the ship's flux dissipation capacity, we can power additional Instructions. The ship dissipates less flux.
liminal_instructions.heavy_armor: By partially phasing the hull's armor into an adjacent dimension, we can increase its effective thickness. We use other dimensions a lot for these Instructions, though we don't really understand what's going on.
liminal_instructions.insulated_engines: Using quantum tunneling principles, we can redirect engine emissions into pocket dimensions. Emissions in other dimensions are harder to detect, for obvious reasons. It's a small price to pay for safety.
liminal_instructions.high_maintenance: To maintain the ship's connection to the Liminality, we need constant reality anchoring. We can make the anchoring more durable, at the cost of increased maintenance. It's a small price to pay for safety (no I did not say that already).
liminal_instructions.flux_shunt: We've discovered a way to shunt hard flux into nothingness, allowing it to dissipate even while shields are raised. The process is much less efficient than normal flux dissipation, but it can work in a pinch!
liminal_instructions.extended_shield: By folding space around the shield emitters, we can extend our shield's coverage. Become invincible! At least until you overload.
liminal_instructions.negative_op: Some Instructions actually simplify the overall template structure, leaving room for more complex ones!
liminal_instructions.negative_cost: We've found a way to create a closed loop in the resource requirements, actually reducing the overall cost of the template. Though the Instruction itself is complex.
liminal_instructions.weapon_range: By compressing the space between our weapons and their targets, we can effectively increase their range. There's no way bending space like this could go wrong!
liminal_instructions.weapon_damage: Using dimensional overlap, we can increase the effective mass and energy of our weapon outputs. Large improvements are beyond us, but every little bit helps.
liminal_instructions.salvage_gantry: By slightly altering probability fields around salvage operations, we can increase the yield of valuable materials. The effect scales with ship size due to the complexity of maintaining larger fields. Try it in a casino!
liminal_instructions.ground_attack: Using localized time dilation, we can multiply the combat output of our marine forces: from inside the field, the battle simply lasts longer. The larger the ship, the more marines the field can cover.
liminal_instructions.bad_turrets: The Liminality disrupts the temporal synchronization between weapon turrets and their targeting systems, reducing their turn rate but leaving more room in the template.
liminal_instructions.maneuverability: By modifying inertial fields, the Liminality improves acceleration, deceleration, and turn rate. Even a capital ship corners like a shuttle.
liminal_instructions.fighter_defense: Incoming damage from any source is diffused across parallel realities, so this reality's fighters take less of it. Their counterparts elsewhere were not consulted.
liminal_instructions.rugged_construction: The Liminality strengthens the conceptual forces binding the ship's materials together, reducing the negative effects of d-mods. That's what this summary says, anyway.
liminal_instructions.fighter_recovery: By manipulating local causality around fighter bays, the Liminality can make it so that some of the pilots we lost were never actually lost. Don't ask about the ethical implications.
liminal_instructions.burn_drive: Unlike existing Alcubierre Drives, our version can now operate in hyperspace! It's not as simple as in normal space, but it works.
liminal_instructions.efficiency: The Liminality fine-tunes molecular interactions across ship systems, so the same work burns less fuel and fewer supplies. The effect reaches everything from drive plumes to ration heaters.
liminal_instructions.cargo_expansion: The Liminality creates localized pockets of expanded space within cargo holds, increasing both cargo and fuel capacity. We recommend unloading before any major template changes.
liminal_instructions.weapon_op_reduction: By optimizing the quantum states of weapon systems, the Liminality reduces the ordnance points required for weapons and fighter wings.
liminal_instructions.missile_reload: The Liminality creates brief causal loops in missile tubes, which allows us to literally unfire missiles and fire them again.
liminal_instructions.fighter_bay: We can construct entire hangar bays in pocket dimensions! Some of the fighter pilots may go insane, but that's a sacrifice we're willing to make.
liminal_instructions.time_flow: As the ship takes damage, the Liminality increasingly warps local time flow, allowing the ship to act more quickly relative to its surroundings. In trials, a frigate on the edge of breakup fought seven subjective minutes in every five.
liminal_instructions.regen: The Liminality reverses entropy in damaged sections of the ship, gradually regenerating hull and armor at rates based on hull size. We tried causal loops first, but the repairs kept arriving before the damage.
liminal_instructions.damage_cap: By diffusing incoming damage across multiple timelines, we can limit how much hull damage the ship takes in a single second. In at least one timeline, this Instruction has already saved your life.
liminal_instructions.glitched_actuators: Some Instructions arrive corrupted, and the weapon actuators mostly run them anyway. We could fix it, but the corrupted copy gives back two whole points of template space.
liminal_instructions.liquid_armor: By relaxing the hull's commitment to the concept of 'solid', armor flows like a liquid, evening itself out across damaged sections.
liminal_instructions.breach_targeting: The Liminality supplies the resonant frequencies of enemy weapon mounts and engine housings, and your targeting computers take it from there.
liminal_instructions.fire_discipline: The Liminality corrects the autofire systems' lead calculations mid-burst. Recoil drops as well, which we did not ask for but will take.
liminal_instructions.close_air_support: Fighters within the ship's conceptual umbrella hit harder. Pilots describe the feeling as 'being watched, but supportively'.
liminal_instructions.flash_repair: The moment battle ends, the Liminality remembers what the ship looked like beforehand and partially reverts it.
liminal_instructions.capacitor_blanking_plates: Empty weapon mounts are capped with plates that dump their unused power feeds back into the flux grid. The fewer guns a ship carries, the more feed there is to reclaim.
liminal_instructions.override_beacon: Nav buoys and comm relays believe this ship has always owned them. It's not mind control if the buoy is happy about it.
liminal_instructions.anchored_firing_solutions: A ship that holds still becomes a fixed point in reality, and fixed points, for reasons still in peer review, shoot faster.

liminal_dialog.planet_win_1: With the swarm defeated, your fleet moves in and deploys the reality anchors. Once placed, they activate and the Entity's hold begins to fail.
liminal_dialog.planet_win_2: Space begins to knit itself back together. Buildings that once defied geometry collapse in on themselves, leaving nothing but empty foundations. The wound seals shut with a soundless flash that reverberates through your being.
liminal_dialog.planet_win_3: What remains is just another lifeless world.
liminal_dialog.planet_loss: You were unable to overcome the swarm.
liminal_dialog.boss_engage_option: Engage the Avatar of the Entity
liminal_dialog.boss_reengage_option: Re-engage the Avatar of the Entity
liminal_dialog.boss_win_1: The Avatar of the Entity comes apart, each fragment guttering out in the dark between dimensions. The connection to the Entity's universe begins to fail, and the wound it opened folds shut behind it with an echo every person in the fleet feels but no instrument records.
liminal_dialog.boss_win_2: As you cross back into normal space, the Entity's defeat is already spreading ahead of you. Every trace of the Servants of the Entity is gone, their fleets and their corrupted worlds with it, as though the Sector had never dreamed them. What they did is not undone. But the doing has stopped.
liminal_dialog.boss_win_3: Back at Galatia Academy, Elna stands before the Liminality, which now pulses with a steadier light. The cradle where Jarn died has been rebuilt. She does not look away from the tesseract this time.
liminal_dialog.boss_win_4: "We've learned so much," she says quietly. "About the Liminality. About the Entity. It will try again, in some other universe if not this one. But its language... we could read scraps of it when this began. We can read whole pages now."
liminal_dialog.boss_win_5: She turns to you with a small smile. "Thank you. Half the Academy called us cranks, and you funded us anyway. Jarn would have been proud."
liminal_dialog.boss_win_reward: All Liminal Templates can now contain 30% more OP of Instructions
liminal_dialog.boss_loss: The Avatar of the Entity defeats you.
